stimulus.title: Exercício B1: Advising Office (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and an academic advisor.

Student: Hi, I wanted to ask about switching one of my electives. I'm in Intro to Statistics, but I'd rather take Data Visualization this term.

Advisor: Let me check... okay, Data Visualization has space. But it has Statistics as a prerequisite — have you completed that?

Student: No, I'm taking it right now. I was hoping to take Data Visualization first and Statistics later.

Advisor: Ah. Unfortunately that's not possible; the prerequisite is enforced by the system. You'd need to finish Statistics first, or get a written waiver from the Data Visualization instructor.

Student: Is it worth asking the instructor directly, or is that rarely approved?

Advisor: It's approved sometimes, especially if you have relevant experience — a coding background, say. Do you have any?

Student: I do, actually — I took two programming courses last year.

Advisor: Then it's worth emailing her. I'll send you her contact information now.

prompt: Gist-purpose. Why does the student visit the advising office?

options.A: To complain about a scheduling conflict between two required courses
options.B: To request a change from one elective to another
options.C: To register for classes for the first time
options.D: To find out why she was removed from a course

explanation: A estudante quer "switch one of my electives". (A) sem conflito de horário; (C) já está matriculada; (D) está fora do que foi dito.

stimulus.title: Exercício B2: Library Reserve Desk (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.

Student: Hi — I'm looking for a book my professor put on reserve for the history seminar. It's The Making of the Atlantic World.

Librarian: Let me look... yes, we have two copies on reserve. Reserve items are two-hour loans, in-library use only. You can't take them out of the building.

Student: Oh. I was hoping to take it home for the weekend — the essay's due Monday.

Librarian: For reserve items, no, sorry. But here's an option: there's a circulating copy in the stacks, on the fourth floor. That one you can take out, for three weeks.

Student: Great, I'll grab that instead. Is it available right now?

Librarian: The catalog says one copy is in. If it's not on the shelf, come back and I'll place a hold on the reserve copy for you to use here.

Student: Thanks — I'll check the stacks first.

prompt: Detail. What is the rule for reserve items?

options.A: They can be borrowed for three weeks
options.B: They are two-hour loans, for use inside the library only
options.C: They cannot be used by undergraduates
options.D: They must be requested 24 hours in advance

explanation: "Two-hour loans, in-library use only... can't take them out of the building." (A) descreve o exemplar da circulação; (C)/(D) não ditos.

stimulus.title: Exercício B3: After Class (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor.

Student: Professor, do you have a minute? I'm a bit lost on the second essay prompt.

Professor: Of course. Which part?

Student: It asks us to "evaluate" the argument, and I'm not sure if that means summarize it or agree or disagree with it.

Professor: Good question — "evaluate" means neither, exactly. It means weigh the argument: where is it strong, where is it weak, and does the evidence actually support the conclusion? You can end up agreeing or disagreeing, but the point is the weighing, not the verdict.

Student: Okay, that helps. So a summary alone wouldn't be enough.

Professor: Right. A summary shows you understood it. Evaluation shows you can think about it. Aim for maybe a third summary, two-thirds evaluation.

Student: Got it. And length — still fifteen hundred words?

Professor: Fifteen hundred, give or take a hundred. Don't pad it.

prompt: Detail. According to the professor, what does "evaluate" mean here?

options.A: Summarize the argument accurately
options.B: Simply agree or disagree with the argument
options.C: Weigh the argument's strengths, weaknesses, and use of evidence
options.D: Compare the argument with another author's

explanation: "Weigh the argument: where is it strong, where is it weak, and does the evidence actually support the conclusion?" (A)/(B) o professor diz que "evaluate" é nenhum dos dois; (D) não dito.

stimulus.title: Exercício B4: Campus Health Clinic (meta de 2 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and a receptionist at the campus health clinic.

Student: Hi, um, I need a nurse to sign this health form for my summer volunteer program. Can I do that today?

Receptionist: Let's see. Have you uploaded your vaccination record to the student health portal yet?

Student: Oh, no, I brought the paper copy with me right here.

Receptionist: Well, our nurses can't sign the form until the file is in the system. You can scan it with your phone and upload it tonight.

Student: Okay, that's easy enough. Do I need an appointment after I upload it?

Receptionist: No, just come back during walk-in hours tomorrow morning between nine and eleven, and a nurse will sign it at the front desk.

prompt: Gist-purpose. Why does the student go to the campus health clinic?

options.A: To get a signature on a required health form
options.B: To schedule a vaccination before summer break
options.C: To pick up a paper copy of her medical record
options.D: To apply for a part-time job at the front desk

explanation: Logo no começo, a estudante explica que precisa que alguém assine o formulário do programa de voluntariado (I need a nurse to sign this health form), o que confirma a opção (A) como pedido de assinatura no documento. Se você pensou em (B), repare que ela já tomou as vacinas e trouxe o comprovante impresso, sem pedir aplicação nova.

stimulus.title: Exercício B5: Dining Services Office (meta de 2 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and a staff member at the dining services office.

Student: Excuse me, I have a question about my campus meal plan. The semester ends in two weeks, and I still have fifteen lunches left.

Staff Member: Are you on the weekly plan or the semester block plan?

Student: Um, the semester block plan, I think. I paid for a hundred meals at the start of the term.

Staff Member: Good news, then. Unused block meals don't expire until the last day of final exams, and you can also trade up to ten of them for coffee shop points.

Student: Oh, nice! I use the library café every morning anyway. How do I make that switch?

Staff Member: Just tap the transfer button in the campus dining app, and the points show up on your ID card right away.

prompt: Detail. What does the staff member say about the student's unused meals?

options.A: They can be refunded for cash at the end of the term
options.B: They expire two weeks before final exams begin
options.C: They are automatically moved to next semester's balance
options.D: They can be partly converted into coffee shop points

explanation: A funcionária explica que o aluno pode trocar até dez refeições restantes por pontos de cafeteria (you can also trade up to ten of them for coffee shop points), o que torna (D) a conversão parcial em pontos. A opção (B) confunde o prazo de duas semanas citado pelo aluno com a regra real, que vale até o último dia de provas finais.

stimulus.title: Exercício B6: Media Equipment Desk (meta de 2 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and an assistant at the media equipment desk.

Student: Hi, I'm recording an interview for my sociology class this afternoon. Do you have a small clip-on microphone I can borrow?

Assistant: Let me check the shelf... sorry, all our clip-on mics are checked out until tomorrow. We do have a handheld digital recorder, though.

Student: Hmm, we're meeting on a bench outside the student union, so I'm worried about wind noise.

Assistant: Actually, this recorder comes with a foam cover that blocks the wind pretty well. You just set it down on the bench between you and your guest.

Student: Oh, great, that'll work. How long can I keep it?

Assistant: It's due back by four p.m. tomorrow. Make sure you check the battery icon on the screen before you start recording.

prompt: Detail. Why can't the student borrow a clip-on microphone today?

options.A: They are reserved for sociology professors only
options.B: They are broken and waiting for repair parts
options.C: They have all been borrowed by other people
options.D: They cannot be used outside the library building

explanation: O atendente confere a prateleira e avisa que todos os microfones de lapela estão emprestados até o dia seguinte (all our clip-on mics are checked out until tomorrow), confirmando (C) como equipamentos já retirados. A opção (A) usa a aula de sociologia mencionada pelo aluno para criar uma restrição que não existe no diálogo.

stimulus.title: Exercício B7: Undergraduate Research Symposium (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and the coordinator of a campus research event.

Student: Hi, Dr. Patel. My lab partner and I were accepted to present our chemistry poster at next month's research symposium, but we just ran into a scheduling issue.

Coordinator: Oh? What happened?

Student: Well, my partner was invited to a regional debate tournament that same weekend, so she won't be on campus. Do we have to withdraw our poster if only one of us can attend?

Coordinator: Not at all. Plenty of co-authored posters are presented by a single student. As long as her name stays on the printed header and the abstract, you're fine to present solo.

Student: That's a huge relief. One more thing, though. I have a Friday afternoon lab that I can't miss. Can I request a morning presentation slot?

Coordinator: Sure, we haven't finalized the room assignments yet. Send me an email by Wednesday so I can put you in the nine-to-eleven session before the program goes to print.

prompt: Gist-purpose. Why did the student go to see the coordinator?

options.A: To ask for extra time to finish a chemistry experiment
options.B: To find out if she can present a joint poster by herself
options.C: To add a new co-author to her research abstract
options.D: To reserve a larger display board for her team's graphs

explanation: A aluna procura o coordenador porque a parceira viajará no fim de semana do evento e quer saber se precisa cancelar o pôster ou se pode apresentar sozinha (Do we have to withdraw our poster if only one of us can attend?), confirmando (B) como dúvida sobre apresentação individual. A opção (C) fala em incluir coautor, mas o nome da colega já estava no trabalho.

stimulus.title: Exercício B8: Environmental Science Office Hours (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and an environmental science professor.

Student: Professor Morales, do you have a minute? I'm worried about my field report on creek water quality.

Professor: Come on in, Leo. Didn't you plan to compare water samples from the wooded bend and the downstream bridge?

Student: That was the plan, yeah, but after Tuesday's heavy rain, the trail to the wooded bend was completely flooded. Park rangers closed it for the rest of the month, so I only have data from the bridge.

Professor: Ah, I heard the creek rose quite a bit. Well, you don't need two locations to write a strong paper. Why not pivot to a before-and-after study at the bridge site alone?

Student: Wait, how would that work? I only started collecting samples there last week.

Professor: The county water board has an automated sensor right under that bridge. Their website posts hourly turbidity and oxygen readings going back five years, so you can compare your post-storm samples with the baseline data from earlier this autumn.

Student: Oh, I had no idea that archive was public! That actually gives me a much clearer research question.

prompt: Detail. What problem prevented the student from carrying out his original plan?

options.A: Heavy rain flooded the path and closed one of his sampling sites
options.B: The testing equipment at the downstream bridge stopped working
options.C: The county water board restricted student access to the creek
options.D: His initial water samples were lost in the laboratory freezer

explanation: O estudante conta que a chuva forte alagou a trilha e levou os guardas-parque a fecharem um dos pontos de coleta (after Tuesday's heavy rain, the trail to the wooded bend was completely flooded), confirmando (A) como interdição da trilha pela chuva. A opção (C) usa o nome do órgão municipal citado depois pela professora para criar uma proibição inexistente.

stimulus.title: Exercício B9: Study Abroad Office (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and a study-abroad advisor.

Student: Hi, I'm applying for the six-week tropical ecology program in Costa Rica this summer, and I wanted to check how the credits transfer back here.

Advisor: Sure. Because that program is run by one of our partner universities, the six credits transfer automatically as general elective hours.

Student: Oh, wait. I was counting on using it to fulfill my upper-level biology lab requirement so I can graduate on time next spring.

Advisor: In that case, automatic transfer won't be enough. You'll need a course-equivalency approval from the chair of our biology department, Dr. Lindqvist.

Student: Okay, what does she usually ask to see? The short course description on the brochure?

Advisor: Actually, she's pretty thorough. A brochure blurb won't cut it. She'll want the full weekly syllabus showing the exact number of field and lab hours, plus how students are graded.

Student: Good to know. The program deposit isn't due until next Friday, so I'll request the detailed syllabus from the host coordinator today.

prompt: Meaning of an expression. What does the advisor mean when he says "A brochure blurb won't cut it"?

options.A: A brief summary from the brochure will not be detailed enough
options.B: The printed brochure contains outdated information about the lab
options.C: The student should not clip pages out of the official catalog
options.D: The biology department no longer accepts summer field courses

explanation: A expressão coloquial won't cut it significa que algo não basta, e o orientador explica logo depois que a chefe do departamento exige o cronograma completo de horas práticas (She'll want the full weekly syllabus), validando (A) como insuficiência do resumo do folheto. A alternativa (C) leva o verbo cut ao pé da letra, como recortar papel.

A opção (A) desiste do intercâmbio sem que o aluno demonstre essa intenção.

stimulus.title: Exercício B10: Architecture Studio Critique (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and an architecture professor after a studio review.

Student: Professor Vance, thanks for staying a few minutes. After the guest panel's critique of my community center model, I'm torn about how to revise the central atrium for the final portfolio.

Professor: You shouldn't feel discouraged, Maya. The visiting architects were genuinely impressed by how your sawtooth roof brings diffused northern light deep into the building.

Student: Right, they liked the daylighting, but they pointed out that placing the quiet reading lounge directly off the open atrium would create an acoustic nightmare whenever groups gather downstairs.

Professor: And that's a fair critique. Concrete floors and glass balustrades bounce sound around. But you don't have to wall off the reading lounge and lose the visual openness that makes your design work.

Student: You mean I can keep the sightlines without enclosing the second floor in glass partitions?

Professor: Exactly. Look into suspended timber baffles along the atrium ceiling and a recessed alcove with fabric wall panels for the reading area. They absorb mid-range chatter before it travels upward, so the space stays visually connected without functioning like an echo chamber.

prompt: Function. Why does the professor mention concrete floors and glass balustrades?

options.A: To encourage the student to replace all glass with brick walls
options.B: To explain why the panel's concern about noise was reasonable
options.C: To show that the building meets local fire safety regulations
options.D: To suggest materials that would make the model easier to build

explanation: Logo após dizer And that's a fair critique, o professor cita o piso de concreto e os guarda-corpos de vidro porque esses materiais refletem o som (bounce sound around), justificando em (B) por que a crítica acústica fazia sentido. Se você marcou (A), repare que ele desaconselha fechar o espaço com paredes logo na frase seguinte.

stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and an architecture professor after a studio review.

Student: Professor Vance, thanks for staying a few minutes. After the guest panel's critique of my community center model, I'm torn about how to revise the central atrium for the final portfolio.

Professor: You shouldn't feel discouraged, Maya. The visiting architects were genuinely impressed by how your sawtooth roof brings diffused northern light deep into the building.

Student: Right, they liked the daylighting, but they pointed out that placing the quiet reading lounge directly off the open atrium would create an acoustic nightmare whenever groups gather downstairs.

Professor: And that's a fair critique. Concrete floors and glass balustrades bounce sound around. But you don't have to wall off the reading lounge and lose the visual openness that makes your design work.

Student: You mean I can keep the sightlines without enclosing the second floor in glass partitions?

Professor: Exactly. Look into suspended timber baffles along the atrium ceiling and a recessed alcove with fabric wall panels for the reading area. They absorb mid-range chatter before it travels upward, so the space stays visually connected without functioning like an echo chamber.

options.A: They will dampen noise while preserving the open view across the atrium
options.B: They will reflect additional sunlight into the downstairs gathering area
options.C: They will divide the reading lounge into private individual study cubicles
options.D: They will support the weight of the sawtooth roof without steel columns

explanation: O professor propõe os defletores de madeira e painéis de tecido porque absorvem as vozes mantendo o espaço integrado visualmente (absorb mid-range chatter... so the space stays visually connected), validando (A) como redução de ruído sem perder a amplitude visual. A alternativa (C) sugere fechar a área em cabines, exatamente o que a aluna queria evitar.

stimulus.title: Exercício B11: Economic History Seminar (meta de 3 min)
stimulus.content:
Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and an economic history professor.

Student: Professor Calloway, I've been going through the digitized county tax rolls from the 1880s for my senior thesis on New England textile towns, and the numbers aren't lining up with what we read in seminar.

Professor: Let me guess. The tax assessments make mill workers' household incomes look surprisingly stable, even during the downturn of 1884?

Student: Exactly! Contemporary newspaper accounts describe widespread layoffs, yet the municipal tax records barely register a dip. Was the press exaggerating?

Professor: Not necessarily. Think about who actually appears on a nineteenth-century property and poll-tax roll. Long-term residents who owned modest cottages or stayed at the same address year-round were recorded, whereas transient operatives and seasonal spinners who left town when looms shut down simply vanished from the assessor's ledger.

Student: Oh, I see. So by relying solely on the tax rolls, I'm only looking at the best-off segment of the workforce that weathered the slump.

Professor: Precisely, it's a classic survivorship bias. If you want to capture the full picture, pair those municipal rolls with the Abbott Mill weekly payroll books in our library's special collections. Those list every piece-rate worker by week, including the ones who disappeared mid-season.

prompt: Detail. According to the professor, why do the county tax rolls make incomes appear stable in 1884?

options.A: Town officials inflated wage figures to attract outside factory investment
options.B: Mill owners continued paying full wages to workers during temporary shutdowns
options.C: Seasonal workers who lost their jobs left town and were omitted from the rolls
options.D: Tax assessors combined factory wages with agricultural earnings from nearby farms

explanation: A professora esclarece que os registros municipais incluíam moradores fixos, enquanto trabalhadores temporários que partiam na crise ficavam de fora (transient operatives and seasonal spinners who left town when looms shut down simply vanished from the assessor's ledger), validando (C) como omissão dos trabalhadores sazonais nos impostos. A alternativa (B) contradiz as demissões relatadas nos jornais.
